rationale: In the documented cohorts of FILIP1-related congenital neuromuscular disorder, mandatory neonatal respiratory distress is absent. In the index cohort of five patients reported by Roos et al. (2023), zero neonates presented with acute neonatal respiratory failure at birth; instead, recurrent respiratory infections were documented later in two of five patients (40%). Furthermore, single case and follow-up studies (such as Watts et al., 2024) document that respiratory insufficiency develops progressively over childhood rather than manifesting universally as neonatal respiratory failure. This markedly contrasts with severe neonatal neuromuscular conditions such as SMARD1, where catastrophic diaphragmatic paralysis and early respiratory distress are quintessential features.

evidence.text: In the primary cohort of five patients with bi-allelic FILIP1 variants, acute neonatal respiratory distress was not reported; rather, recurrent respiratory infections developed later in two of the five individuals.
